source.how: get_computed_styles for the declared values; get_node_info / get_children for the laid-out rects of 'Slider inline / md / Dot size' and its label and value, whose world coordinates are what `gaps` is computed from.

note: The inline bar is the one figure in Slider whose spacing is authored by padding rather than by the thumb-inset arithmetic SLIDER_SIZE documents: label and value sit INSIDE a 40px bar, 12px in from each end, 8px apart, centred vertically. It is measured on the content row (slider-content), which is laid over the bar at inset 0 — so its border box IS the bar's. The fill and the 2px handle are absolutely positioned under it and are not part of the figure.

lawsNotDeclared.uniform-inset: Not uniform by design: 12px inline (space-md), and the block inset is whatever centring a 13px line in a 40px field leaves — 11 on the sheet, 11.2 rendered.
lawsNotDeclared.inset-is-declared: Only the inline sides are padding. The block inset is authored by align-items: center inside h-field-md, so declaring it as padding would make the field height a second author of the same number.
lawsNotDeclared.concentric-radius: The children are unboxed text with no radius of their own; the bar's radius-md has nothing inside it to be concentric with.
